newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Azerbaijan fail to end radar station row.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Azerbaijan fail to end radar station row.

text.p: Russia and Azerbaijan have failed to reach agreement on the use of a former Soviet early-warning radar station on Azerbaijan's territory and will have to hold more talks to resolve the dispute.

Interfax news agency said Azeri President Haydar Aliyev and Russian Defense Minister Igor Sergeyev had failed to agree terms for using the Gaballa radar station, in northern Azerbaijan, during talks in Moscow on Thursday.

The status of the station, set up by the Soviet union to warn of inter-continental ballistic missile attacks from abroad, has been unclear since the break up of the superpower in 1991. A team of 400 Russian military experts operates it.
Interfax said the two men had agreed to set up a joint commission which would try to reach a final agreement. It said a deal to create the commission could be signed on Friday.
"We have given a group of our experts the task of drawing up an appropriate document about the future existence of this station," Interfax quoted Aliyev as telling reporters on Thursday.
Aliyev, on a three-day state visit to Russia, has previously said his country is not opposed to the presence of the station.

Baku has in the past said Russia must pay $70 million in unpaid electricity bills for Gaballa. It also wants the issue of allegedly high rates of disease and infant mortality in communities nearby to be addressed.
Russia regards the station as vital to its security and is anxious to secure a deal.

"A lot of money has been invested in the station and it works not only for Russia but for the countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States," Sergeyev said, referring to the loose grouping of 12 former Soviet republics.
Azerbaijan has been a member of a CIS collective security pact since autumn 1994.
Sergeyev said the radar station, the last Russian military installation on Azeri territory, should function for many years to come.

Aliyev also met Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday. Yeltsin promised to intensify Russian mediating efforts at finding a solution to Azerbaijan's long-running dispute with neighbouring Armenia over the territory of Nagorno-Karabakh.
